subject: Peninsula expansion — price stabilizer & temporary credit handoff
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Dunn <sophie@peninsularetail.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Peninsula expansion — price stabilizer & temporary credit handoff

Hi Sophie —

Quick follow from our renewal planning call this morning. Peninsula's usage growth looks like it will push you into the next tier in Q4; Sophie mentioned wanting to lock unit economics while ramping the new personalization work. To keep things predictable for your finance team, I attached a short proposal (Peninsula_MA_PLAN_v2.pdf) and an editable pricing_model.xlsx that sketches two pathways:

- Option A: 12-month term, baseline commit +40% with a 6-month temporary price hold at current unit rate, then reprice thereafter.
- Option B: 24-month term with stepped discounts (5% year 1, 8% year 2) and bridging credits applied on the first three invoices.

We can also apply a $50k bridging credit to offset onboarding/embedding compute for the first 90 days if Peninsula signs by July 15. That credit would be invoiced as an invoice credit (not a refund) and documented in an amendment.

Ask: could you confirm which option your procurement prefers and whether a 60-day PO/Net60 term is required? If you want, I can loop in legal/finance to draft an amendment and a DocuSign envelope.

Thanks —
Mateo
Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Peninsula_MA_PLAN_v2.pdf, pricing_model.xlsx
From: Sophie Dunn <sophie@peninsularetail.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv.mehta@peninsularetail.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@peninsularetail.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Peninsula expansion — price stabilizer & temporary credit handoff

Hi Mateo —

Thanks for the clear options and the model — I reviewed with Rajiv and procurement. A few points from our side:

1) We prefer a shorter term for flexibility (Option A looks better) but we need the price protection to run for 9 months instead of 6 so we can complete current pilot integrations.
2) The $50k credit is attractive — can it be split across invoices (first 90 days looks fine).
3) Procurement requires Net60 on invoices and a signed amendment (legal needs to review redlines).
4) We also want a performance SLA clause: 99.5% availability and a token-cost cap for embedding calls in high-volume windows.

If you can confirm the 9-month hold + Net60 and send an amendment draft, we can escalate internally for PO.

Best,
Sophie Dunn
VP Product, Peninsula Retail
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sophie Dunn <sophie@peninsularetail.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Peninsula expansion — need approval on 9-month hold and Net60

Lauren, Priyom —

Forwarding Sophie and Rajiv's reply. Peninsula wants: 9-month price hold (vs our proposed 6), $50k bridging credit split across first three invoices, Net60 payment terms, and SLA/token-cost cap asks. They prefer Option A (12-month with commit +40%).

Questions:
- Legal: is a 9-month temporary price hold permissible contractually (we've typically done 6 months)? Can we add a limited SLA clause referencing Console metrics (latency/availability) without broadening warranty risk?
- Sales Ops: can we structure the $50k as an invoice credit to be amortized over the first 3 monthly invoices? Any billing system gotchas with Net60 + credit timing?

If acceptable, I'd like to offer the 9-month hold conditioned on signed amendment + PO by July 15. If not, what's the minimum we can approve without exec sign-off?

Thanks —
Mateo
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sophie Dunn <sophie@peninsularetail.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Peninsula expansion — need approval on 9-month hold and Net60

Mateo —

We can accept the 9-month temporary price hold as a one-off commercial concession. Conditions to document in the amendment:

- Price hold is timeboxed (effective from go-live date for 9 months), after which the agreed-for reprice schedule applies.
- Bridging credit ($50,000) to be applied as invoice credit across first three invoices; credit is non-recoverable and will be reflected in the first invoice statements.
- Net60 payment terms allowed; Redwood will treat the invoices as Net60 but will require a PO referencing the amendment.
- SLA language: reference our Console SLOs (99.5% monthly availability) and include a carve-out for force majeure and scheduled maintenance; do not add financial penalties — instead, include remediation and crediting process so we limit warranty exposure.

We have a ConcessionMatrix_v1.xlsx (attached) that sets approval thresholds. This package is within C-level delegated authority so no additional exec sign-off required. Legal can draft Amendment_v1.docx for signature; once PO + signed amendment received, finance can schedule the invoice credits.

I will prepare the amendment and loop in legal for redlines.

—Lauren
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: ConcessionMatrix_v1.xlsx
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Dunn <sophie@peninsularetail.com>, Rajiv Mehta <rajiv.mehta@peninsularetail.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@peninsularetail.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 16:38:00 -0700
Subject: Peninsula amendment & next steps (DocuSign link)

Sophie / Rajiv —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per Lauren's guidance, Redwood will: 1) apply a 9-month price hold starting on go-live, 2) issue a $50k bridging credit across the first three invoices, and 3) accept Net60 payment terms with a PO referencing the amendment. The SLA language will reference Console SLOs with remediation-based credits (no penalties).

I've attached Amendment_v1.docx. Legal has pre-populated the DocuSign envelope; please sign the amendment and upload the PO. Link: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/Envelope/ABC-123-DEF

Next steps:
- Peninsula to countersign amendment via DocuSign by Jul 15 to secure the bridging credit.
- Procurement to issue PO for the committed baseline by invoice date.
- Finance will apply the $50k credit across invoices 1–3 after PO and signed amendment are received.

If you want any small edits to the amendment before we send to DocuSign, reply-all and we can have legal make the change quickly. Appreciate the collaboration — excited to scale with you.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Amendment_v1.docx
